ruled 2026-09-27 by Jens Nordmark (@nordmarj): the Caribbean Netherlands takes GADM. It draws all four islands - Bonaire, Klein Bonaire, Saba and Sint Eustatius - with 0.18 px between vertices and 323.7 km2 against the published 322, and fails only the ground test (2.07 px of edge), against a weak consensus: Natural Earth at 9.75 px between vertices, geoBoundaries at 243 km2 (which fails too), and Overture, which draws only Bonaire and Klein Bonaire and misses Saba and Sint Eustatius entirely - the one passing source, and 18.3 px between vertices, over the 4 px cap, so the rule alone would keep Natural Earth

ruled 2026-09-27 by Jens Nordmark (@nordmarj): Hong Kong takes a source that draws its islands, and the World Bank draws the territory best. No source passes (all three fail ground, 1.1-1.6 px of edge apart), and Natural Earth, at 1,036 km2 against the published 1,105.69 km2 of land, lacks some 25 islands both other sources draw, Chek Lap Kok among them (20.7 km2, 35 px across on the card). Of the two that draw them, Overture is closer in area (1,104.8 km2) but its land polygon is a set of straight facets: 81% of its perimeter lies in segments longer than 4 card pixels (the longest 11.3 km), against 6% of the World Bank's (the longest 2.8 km), so Tolo Harbour is a sliver cut through the New Territories and Lantau a polygon - its 18 m median vertex spacing is dense noding along those facets. The World Bank draws a plausible coast, 1,089.9 km2 (-1.4%) at 1.75 px between vertices, within the 4 px cap; renders compared side by side on 2026-09-27

ruled 2026-10-27 by Jens Nordmark (@nordmarj): the Republic of the Congo takes the World Bank's outline. Natural Earth passes the three tests, but Overture Maps 2026-09-23.1, which draws the subdivision cards, redrew the Sangha and Kouilou borders onto the World Bank's line (CG-7 gave about 126 km2 near 16.50 E, 2.90 N to the Central African Republic's CF-SE, CG-9 about 81 km2 near 11.89 E, 3.48 S to Gabon's GA-5, a point check against the World Bank's version 3 agreeing on both), and Natural Earth's line, a few km off along the Sangha and the Ubangi, left slivers and double lines on every Congo card. The World Bank passes all three tests, 342,701 km2 against the published 342,000 - the passing source closest to it, the one the closest-area rule would pick were Natural Earth to fail - at 0.11 px between vertices, within the 4 px cap, and misses no island (measured 2026-10-27; the card has none)

ruled 2026-09-27 by Jens Nordmark (@nordmarj): Turkmenistan keeps Natural Earth. GADM, geoBoundaries and Overture Maps pass the three tests, and all three draw the Garabogazkol lagoon as land (Natural Earth 470,850 km2 against geoBoundaries 491,430); the published 491,210 km2 is land and water together, so the closest-area rule is misled by the lagoon and took geoBoundaries, and the card drew the lagoon red. Natural Earth is the source that leaves the lagoon out as water, which the internal-waters rule (2026-09-25: internal waters are tinted like the sea zone) then tints as Turkmenistan's; the World Bank leaves it out too, and the two are the ones that fail ground and position (Natural Earth 1.6 px of edge, 6.0 px off). Found on the rendered card on 2026-09-27; the subdivision card drawing the same lagoon as land (GADM's Balkan, TKM.3_1) is cut in subdivision_water.tsv under the same ruling.
